title: Coupled bound for averaged indicators
statement:
Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and take $u,v\in\mathbb R$ and $x,x'\in\mathbb R^n$. If $Y,Y'$ are independent standard Gaussian vectors in $\mathbb R^n$, then
\[
|u_u(x)-u_u(\cos v\,x+\sin v\,x')|
\le \Pr\!\left(1_A(\cos u\,x+\sin u\,Y)\ne 1_A\bigl(\cos u(\cos v\,x+\sin v\,x')+\sin u(\cos v\,Y+\sin v\,Y')\bigr)\right),
\]
where $u_u(w)=\int 1_A(\cos u\,w+\sin u\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$.
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. Let $A$ be measurable, $u,v\in\mathbb R$, and $x,x\prime\in\mathbb R^n$. For independent $Y,Y\prime\sim\gamma_n$, $|u_u(x)-u_u(\cos v\,x+\sin v\,x\prime)|\le\Pr(1_A(\cos u\,x+\sin u\,Y)\ne1_A(\cos u(\cos v\,x+\sin v\,x\prime)+\sin u(\cos v\,Y+\sin v\,Y\prime)))$.
